{{Short description|French physicist}}

[[File:Emmanuel Desurvire, Budapest, European Inventor Award, 2011.jpg|thumb|Emmanuel Desurvire]]
'''Emmanuel Desurvire''' (born 1955) is a French researcher and writer. He is the recipient of 2007 [[John Tyndall Award]].

==Early life==
Desurvire was born in 1955, in [[Boulogne]], France to Raymond Desurvire, an [[Aircraft maintenance technician|aircraft engineer]] and Marcelle Desurvire, a [[psychologist]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.encyclopedia.com/arts/educational-magazines/desurvire-emmanuel-1955|title=Desurvire, Emmanuel 1955|website=Encyclopedia.com|access-date=3 July 2022}}</ref>

Desurvire attended [[University of Paris]] where he received his M.S. degree in theoretical physics in 1981 and [[University of Nice]], where he completed his Ph.D. in 1983.<ref name="auto"/>

==Career==
In 2005, he was awarded with the William Streifer Scientific Achievement Award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.optica.org/en-us/history/biographies/bios/emmanuel_desurvire/|title=Emmanuel Desurvire &#124; Living History  |website=Optica.org|access-date=3 July 2022}}</ref>

In 1998, he received [[Franklin Institute Awards|Benjamin Franklin Medal]].

In 2007, he received [[John Tyndall Award]] for his contributions in the development of [[Erbium-doped fiber amplifier]]s.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.photonicssociety.org/awards/john-tyndall-award/john-tyndall-award-winners | title=John Tyndall Award Winners - IEEE Photonics Society|website=Photonicssociety.org}}</ref>

==Awards==
* 2007: [[John Tyndall Award]]
* 2022: [[VinFuture Grand Prize]]
